newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - strict adherence to EMU criteria crucial.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - strict adherence to EMU criteria crucial.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said strict adherence to the criteria which countries must fulfil to launch Europe's planned common currency was crucial for a stable euro.

"Strict adherence to the stability criteria is a decisive prerequisite for a strong euro," Waigel told the Welt am Sonntag newspaper. A copy of the article to be published on Sunday was released in advance.
Waigel also said Germany would make every effort to meet the criteria and the chances it would do so were good.
"Germans will only accept the common European currency if it is just as strong as the mark. Therefore I stand by my statement -- convergence determines the timetable," Waigel said.
Talk of a laxity on the Maastricht criteria risked ruining confidence in the euro and supporters of a delayed euro launch "added to disturbances on financial markets," Waigel said.

The Maastricht Treaty calls on contenders for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) to keep their budget deficits at or below three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and says debt levels should not exceed 60 percent of GDP.
There has been mounting concern that Germany will not meet the budget criteria as it wrestles with record unemployment levels which are sapping tax returns and inflating social security spending.
Earlier, top economic institute DIW urged Bonn to take advantage of the leeway allowed for in the Maastricht Treaty to ensure EMU goes ahead on time.
Waigel said that he was still determined to achieve more cuts in social welfare spending. "Budgetary consolidation is a very serious issue for me," he said.
This was "not a duty exercise for Maastricht but is happening in our own interests," he said. Structural reforms were essential in order to secure more growth, spending and create jobs.
